deck_title: Airy-Stokes infinite multi-bounce glass pane rational series vs naive double-surface 2R blowout rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic George Biddell Airy (1833) & George Gabriel Stokes (1862) infinite internal reflection geometric series for a two-surface thin dielectric pane (summing R_pane = R + T^2*R/(1-R^2) = 2R/(1+R) and T_pane = T^2/(1-R^2) = (1-R)/(1+R) across 17 single-interface Fresnel reflectance stations R = u in [0.0000, 1.0000] to lock total pane energy E = 2R/(1+R) + (1-R)/(1+R) = 1.0000x with 0/17 violated stations) versus naive unattenuated double-surface addition (R_naive = 2R, T_naive = 1 - R, which inflates total energy as 1 + R to 1.2500x at R=0.25, 1.5000x at R=0.50, and 2.0000x / 200% glowing rim at grazing R=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-bounce geometric ray-tracing series.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Architectural window panes, automotive windshields, and thin-wall glass shaders (glTF KHR_materials_transmission)
Soap bubbles, thin ice sheets, and visor shields where front and back interfaces are unresolved in a single mesh layer
Grazing-angle glass reflectance smoothly saturating at 2R/(1+R) -> 1.0000 instead of 2R -> 2.0000
Closed-form infinite internal bounce summation without recursive ray-tracing loops
not_for: Thick refractive solid spheres or lenses where front and back surfaces have different normals and refract rays along divergent paths

dark_box.lead: MIT original code. Synthetic educational scene; local checks reproduced. No production, physics, or neural inference certification.
